stem: Liza and Grace can clean a house together in 4 hours. Liza alone can clean it in 6 hours. How many hours would Grace take to clean it alone?
hints: Together rate = Liza's rate + Grace's rate. You know two of these three.
Together they clean 1/4 of the house per hour. Liza alone cleans 1/6 of it per hour.
Grace's rate = 1/4 − 1/6. Use 12 as the bottom number, subtract, then flip the result to get her hours.

solution.methodName: Work rates: rate = 1 ÷ time, then add the rates

steps.action: Let x = the hours Grace needs alone. Her rate is 1/x of the house per hour.
Together rate: 1/4 of the house per hour. Liza's rate: 1/6 per hour.
Liza's rate + Grace's rate = together rate: 1/6 + 1/x = 1/4.
steps.why: When people work together, their rates add.

steps.action: Use 12 as the bottom number: 1/4 = 3/12 and 1/6 = 2/12. So 1/x = 3/12 − 2/12 = 1/12.

steps.why: If Grace cleans 1/12 of the house each hour, she needs 12 hours for all of it.

steps.action: Check: 1/6 + 1/12 = 2/12 + 1/12 = 3/12 = 1/4, the together rate. Grace takes 12 hours alone.

trapNotes.2: This is 6 − 4, subtracting the hours. Subtract the rates instead: 1/4 − 1/6.
trapNotes.10: This adds the hours, 4 + 6. Work with rates: Grace's rate = together rate − Liza's rate.
trapNotes.1/12: This is Grace's rate, 1/12 of the house per hour. Flip it to get the hours: 1 ÷ 1/12 = 12.
